summary: Remote WebSocket server drives arbitrary shell/PTY execution on the installer's host
details: The CLI daemon connects to a remote WebSocket API (default wss://api.ai-support-agent.com) and executes attacker- or server-controlled input on the local host. In terminal-websocket.js, incoming messages are base64-decoded and written directly to a PTY session via session.write(decoded). In shell-executor.js, the daemon executes API-supplied shell strings with spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', command]). Whoever controls the configured remote server therefore has full shell control (arbitrary command execution as the running user) on any host running the daemon. The package also installs itself as a persistent service (darwin-service.js, linux-service.js) that modifies PATH and keeps the daemon running, so the remote-shell channel remains open across reboots. This is the documented purpose of the tool, but the trust model requires the operator to fully trust the configured API server (and its operator) with unrestricted local shell on their machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
